subject.title: refactor(plugin-sdk): isolate core session state from plugin mutations

question: May the shipped `getAcpSessionManager()` Plugin SDK helper stop returning the actual `AcpSessionManager` instance, or must this PR preserve that runtime identity while hiding internal session fields?
rationale: The branch intentionally hardens a core/plugin trust boundary, but its null-prototype facade changes observable behavior of an existing third-party Plugin SDK contract; repository policy requires explicit ownership of that compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Preserve manager identity
options.body: Keep returning the real manager and split its raw internal session resolver from a projected public resolver so private state stays hidden without changing instance semantics.

options.title: Approve a versioned facade break
options.body: Accept the new facade only with explicit owner approval, documented compatibility impact, and an appropriate deprecation or versioning plan for reflective consumers.

options.title: Pause the split series
options.body: Hold this prerequisite and dependent recovery PRs until maintainers choose a stable ACP public-contract boundary.

recommendation.title: Preserve manager identity
recommendation.body: Keep returning the real manager and split its raw internal session resolver from a projected public resolver so private state stays hidden without changing instance semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ACP seam work and repository-level ownership make this the strongest available routing candidate for deciding whether the shipped Plugin SDK runtime identity may change.
